name: create_expectation
description: Creates a mock expectation that defines how MockServer should respond to a matching request. It accepts no other parameters than those in its input schema: an unknown one is rejected with an error naming it. Use raw_expectation to match request headers, query parameters, cookies or a body, or to add a delay or a template.

method.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.)

responseBody.description: Response body as string or object

times.description: Number of times this expectation should match

chaos.description: Declarative HTTP chaos/fault injection profile for probabilistic errors, latency, and count-based stateful faults

errorStatus.description: HTTP status to inject on error (e.g. 500, 503, 429)

retryAfter.description: Optional Retry-After header value on injected error

dropConnectionProbability.description: Probability (0.0-1.0) of dropping the TCP connection without sending any response

seed.description: Optional seed for reproducible probabilistic draws

succeedFirst.description: First N matches are NOT eligible for chaos (>= 0)

failRequestCount.description: After succeedFirst, next M matches ARE eligible for chaos (>= 1)

outageAfterMillis.description: Time-based outage window: chaos becomes active this many ms after the first match (>= 0)

outageDurationMillis.description: Time-based outage window: chaos stays active for this many ms then self-heals (>= 1)

truncateBodyAtFraction.description: Corrupt the response body by keeping only this leading fraction (0.0-1.0) of its bytes

malformedBody.description: Corrupt the response body by appending a broken-JSON fragment so it fails to parse

slowResponseChunkSize.description: Dribble the response body in chunks of this many bytes (>= 1); requires slowResponseChunkDelay

quotaName.description: Stateful quota: shared counter key; expectations with the same quotaName share one rate-limit counter

quotaLimit.description: Stateful quota: max requests allowed per window before requests are rejected (>= 1)

quotaWindowMillis.description: Stateful quota: fixed-window length in milliseconds (>= 1)

quotaErrorStatus.description: Stateful quota: status returned when the quota is exceeded (default 429)

degradationRampMillis.description: Gradual degradation: ramp errorProbability and dropConnectionProbability from 0 to full over this many milliseconds from the first match (>= 1)

name: verify_request
description: Verifies that a request matching the specified criteria was received a certain number of times

atLeast.description: Minimum number of matching requests expected

atMost.description: Maximum number of matching requests expected

name: retrieve_recorded_requests
description: Retrieves recorded requests that were received by MockServer, optionally filtered by method and path

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return (default 50)

name: retrieve_logs
description: Retrieve MockServer's recorded log messages — request matching, mismatches, actions and errors — to debug why a test/request behaved as it did. Returns structured LOG_ENTRIES format. Use the correlationId filter to narrow to a single request's lifecycle.

correlationId.description: Filter to a single request's log entries by its correlation ID — the key debugging filter. Each incoming request is assigned a unique correlation ID that links all log entries for that request's lifecycle.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (default 100, max 500). Returns the most recent entries when more are available.

name: clear_expectations
description: Clears expectations and/or recorded requests from MockServer matching the specified criteria

type.description: What to clear: ALL, LOG, or EXPECTATIONS

name: reset
description: Resets MockServer by clearing all expectations, recorded requests, and logs

name: manage_service_chaos
description: Manage service-scoped HTTP chaos: register one chaos profile per upstream host (applied to all matched forwards to that host that have no chaos of their own), remove a host's profile, or clear all. The host-keyed profiles are applied on the matched-forward path; an expectation's own chaos always takes precedence.

action.description: One of: register (set a host's chaos), remove (clear one host), clear (clear all)

host.description: Upstream host to break (required for register/remove); matched case-insensitively, ignoring any :port

chaos.description: The HttpChaosProfile to apply (required for register): same fields as the create_expectation 'chaos' block (errorStatus, errorProbability, dropConnectionProbability, latency, truncateBodyAtFraction, malformedBody, slowResponseChunkSize/Delay, quota*, degradationRampMillis, etc.)

ttlMillis.description: Optional time-to-live for a 'register': the chaos auto-reverts after this many ms (a dead-man's switch so chaos self-heals if no clear is sent). Omit for chaos that persists until explicitly cleared.

name: get_status
description: Returns the current status of MockServer including listening ports and running state

name: verify_request_sequence
description: Verifies that requests were received in the specified order

requests.description: Ordered list of requests to verify in sequence

name: retrieve_request_responses
description: Retrieves request-response pairs that were recorded by MockServer

limit.description: Maximum number of pairs to return (default 50)

name: create_forward_expectation
description: Creates a forward/proxy expectation that forwards matching requests to a specified host

path.description: Request path to match for forwarding

scheme.description: Scheme for forwarding: HTTP or HTTPS (default HTTPS)

name: debug_request_mismatch
description: Analyzes why a request does not match any active expectations, showing per-field match failures for each expectation

method.description: HTTP method of the request to debug

path.description: Path of the request to debug

headers.description: Headers of the request to debug

body.description: Body of the request to debug

name: explain_unmatched_requests
description: Returns recent requests that hit MockServer and matched no expectation, with ranked closest-expectation diagnostics and actionable remediation hints for each mismatch. Use after a failed test run to understand why requests got 404s without needing to reconstruct the request. A request MockServer forwarded or proxied that failed with a 502 is not listed: explain_forward_failure explains it.

limit.description: Maximum number of unmatched requests to return (default 10, max 100)

name: explain_request
description: Explains one request MockServer has already received, identified by its correlation id: which expectation would serve it now, why each expectation evaluated ahead of that one was passed over (NAMESPACE, INACTIVE, FIELDS_DIFFER with per-field differences and remediation hints, CONVERSATION, SCENARIO_STATE, PERCENTAGE), which lower-priority expectations it shadows, and the outcome when it arrived, with atArrival.forwardFailure giving the reason when its forward failed with a 502. Recomputed now against the current expectations without consuming Times or moving scenarios; says whether the expectations changed since. Recorded values are redacted as in the event log (redactSecretsInLog). Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/explain?correlationId=<id>.

correlationId.description: Correlation id of one request MockServer has received, as shown by retrieve_logs (each log entry carries it) or the dashboard log

name: diagnose_config
description: Reports MockServer's effective configuration: each mockserver.* property set away from its default, its value, the source that supplied it (system-property, properties-file, environment-variable or runtime-set) and its built-in default ('default', when known). Pass 'name' to check whether a particular setting took effect. Also lists each unrecognised mockserver.* / MOCKSERVER_* key, which MockServer ignores, by name only with the property it was probably meant to be, or marked removed for a property removed in 9.0.0. Credential values are always redacted. Reports the same values and sources as GET /mockserver/config, which lists every property.

name.description: Optional property name or fragment to look up, in any form (maxExpectations, mockserver.maxExpectations or MOCKSERVER_MAX_EXPECTATIONS); returns every matching property, including those at their default with the default's value. Without it, only the properties set away from their default are returned.

name: explain_forward_failure
description: Explains why MockServer could not forward or proxy a request: returns the recorded failed forwards (most recent first, or the one with 'correlationId'), each with its method, path, status code and the reason its 502 gave. MockServer names the cause and what to change when it can (causeNamed true): a TLS failure, an HTTP/2 error, a connection it could not set up, an upstream response it could not decode, an unresolvable host, a refused or timed-out connection, no route, local ports or files running out, an unreachable upstream proxy, a pooled connection closed under a non-idempotent request; forwardLoopSuspected is true when the forward went back to MockServer itself. Reasons are redacted as in the event log (redactSecretsInLog). Failed forwards are recorded only at logLevel INFO or more detailed.

correlationId.description: Optional correlation id of one request whose forward failed, as shown by retrieve_logs; without it, the most recent failed forwards are returned

limit.description: How many of the most recent failed forwards to return when no correlationId is given (default 5, max 20)

name: test_template
description: Dry-runs a Velocity, Mustache or JavaScript response or forward template against a sample request without creating an expectation, using the server's own engines, sandbox and time limit. Returns the rendered response or request, or the failure with its template line and column and a hint, plus warnings for unresolved Velocity references and scenario.set calls (reported, never applied). Nothing reaches the event log. It runs the template code it is sent, so it needs the same mutate role as PUT /mockserver/template/test, which it is equivalent to.

template.description: The template text, as it would appear in an httpResponseTemplate or httpForwardTemplate

actionType.description: RESPONSE_TEMPLATE (default) renders a response; FORWARD_TEMPLATE renders the request to forward

request.description: Optional sample request in MockServer's JSON request format (method, path, queryStringParameters, headers, body); defaults to GET /

name: lint_expectations
description: Lints expectations for mistakes that make them never match or never answer: an expectation shadowed by an earlier one, times / time to live / percentage of 0, unreachable sequential responses, path mistakes (no leading slash, a scheme and host or a query string in the path, a glob wildcard, an OpenAPI {param} with no path parameters), method and header-name typos, duplicate ids, invalid expectations (error) and STRICT JSON bodies with arrays (info). Lints the active expectations, or the ones passed in without storing them. Advisory only: nothing is rejected or changed. Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/lint.

expectations.description: Optional expectation, or array of expectations, in MockServer's JSON format to lint without storing them; without it, the active expectations are linted

maxIssues.description: Most issues to return, errors first (default 100, max 1000); the counts always cover every issue found

name: suggest_expectation_fix
description: For each recent request that matched no expectation, suggests a fix to each of its five closest expectations: a guarded RFC 6902 JSON patch of the expectation, as list_expectations returns it, that changes only its httpRequest so it would match, the fields it could not patch with a reason, and matchesAfterPatch. Each change is preceded by a test of the current value, so the patch fails if the expectation changed since. Nothing is applied: to apply one, patch the expectation's JSON and send it with raw_expectation keeping its id. Values the event log redacts are never copied into a patch. Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/explainUnmatched with "suggestFixes": true, keeping only the expectations with a suggested fix.

limit.description: How many of the most recent unmatched requests to suggest fixes for (default 5, max 20)

expectationId.description: Optional: only suggest fixes to this expectation

name: create_expectation_from_openapi
description: Creates expectations from an OpenAPI specification, optionally specifying which operations and response codes to use. loadProblems lists where a spec that loaded breaks the OpenAPI rules (kind, JSON-pointer location, description, hint), which can stop parts of it working as expected; at most 50 are listed, and loadProblemsNotShown counts the rest

specUrlOrPayload.description: OpenAPI spec URL or JSON/YAML payload

operationsAndResponses.description: Map of operationId to response status code (string) or object with statusCode and optional exampleName

contextPathPrefix.description: Optional path prefix to prepend to all OpenAPI spec paths

name: create_expectations_from_recorded_traffic
description: Converts traffic already recorded by MockServer's forwarding/proxy mode into active mock expectations in one step. After observing a real API via a forwarding proxy, call this tool to generate expectations that replay the recorded responses. Use preview=true to inspect the expectations before committing, or leave it false (default) to activate them immediately.

method.description: Filter recorded traffic by HTTP method (e.g. GET, POST)

path.description: Filter recorded traffic by request path (e.g. /api/users)

preview.description: When true, return the generated expectations as JSON without adding them. Defaults to false.

name: stop_server
description: Stops the MockServer instance

name: raw_expectation
description: Creates an expectation using the full MockServer JSON format, supporting all features including templates, callbacks, and overrides

expectation.description: Full expectation JSON in MockServer format

name: raw_retrieve
description: Retrieves data from MockServer using the full retrieve API with complete control over type, format, and correlation ID filtering

correlationId.description: Filter log entries by correlation ID (only applies when type is LOGS)

name: raw_verify
description: Performs request verification using the full MockServer verification JSON format

verification.description: Full verification JSON in MockServer format

name: verify_traffic_against_openapi
description: Verify the API calls already recorded by MockServer conform to an OpenAPI contract. Pulls recorded request-response pairs from the event log, validates each against the spec, and returns a per-pair conformance report with request and response validation errors.

specUrlOrPayload.description: OpenAPI spec as a URL, file path, or inline JSON/YAML payload

method.description: Filter recorded traffic by HTTP method (e.g. GET, POST)

path.description: Filter recorded traffic by request path (e.g. /api/users)

name: run_contract_test
description: Send example requests derived from an OpenAPI spec to a running service and check the responses conform — use this to verify a service you just built or changed. Builds representative requests for each operation (path parameters, query parameters, headers, request body) from spec examples and schema defaults, sends them to the specified base URL, and validates each response against the spec. Each request has a 10-second timeout.

specUrlOrPayload.description: OpenAPI spec as a URL, file path, or inline JSON/YAML payload

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the service under test (e.g. http://localhost:8080)

operationId.description: Optional filter to test only a specific operation by operationId

name: run_resiliency_test
description: Send malformed and boundary-case requests derived from an OpenAPI spec to a running service and report which inputs it failed to handle gracefully — use this to verify the error handling of a service you built or changed. Generates mutations such as omitting required fields, type violations, numeric and string boundary violations, and malformed JSON bodies. Each request has a 5-second timeout so unresponsive endpoints are classified as UNEXPECTED promptly.

specUrlOrPayload.description: OpenAPI spec as a URL, file path, or inline JSON/YAML payload

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the service under test (e.g. http://localhost:8080)

operationId.description: Optional filter to test only a specific operation by operationId

name: run_mcp_contract_test
description: Check that a target MCP (Model Context Protocol) server correctly implements the protocol over Streamable HTTP — use this to verify an MCP server you built or changed. Runs the required JSON-RPC handshake and core methods against the endpoint (initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, and unknown-method rejection) and validates the shape of each response (JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope, required result fields), never the semantics of any tool. Optionally exercises one tools/call. Each request has a 10-second timeout (so up to ~60 seconds total across all checks).

targetUrl.description: Full URL of the target MCP server's Streamable HTTP endpoint (e.g. http://localhost:1080/mockserver/mcp)

protocolVersion.description: MCP protocol version to advertise during initialize (default 2025-06-18; use e.g. 2025-03-26 to test an older revision)

toolName.description: Optional tool to exercise via a tools/call shape check; omit to skip (a tools/call may have side effects on the target)

name: record_llm_fixtures
description: Snapshots LLM/MCP traffic recorded through MockServer's forwarding proxy into a committable, secret-free fixture file for deterministic replay. Converts recorded request-response pairs (including SSE streaming responses from APIs like Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, etc.) into MockServer expectations with secrets (Authorization, api-key, etc.) automatically redacted from headers. JSON body fields are redacted too when named via redactBodyFields or the mockserver.fixtureBodyRedactFields config; otherwise bodies are left intact, so review fixtures before committing if your app puts credentials in bodies. The output file uses MockServer's standard expectation JSON format and can be loaded with load_expectations_from_file or via initializationJsonPath.

path.description: File path to write the fixture JSON to. The directory must exist.

host.description: Optional filter: only include recorded traffic whose request host matches this value

requestPath.description: Optional filter: only include recorded traffic whose request path matches this value

redactBodyFields.description: Optional JSON field names whose values are redacted from request/response bodies (in addition to sensitive headers and the mockserver.fixtureBodyRedactFields config)

name: load_expectations_from_file
description: Loads expectations from a JSON fixture file and adds them as active mock expectations in MockServer. Use this to replay LLM/MCP traffic previously recorded with record_llm_fixtures. The file must contain expectations in MockServer's standard JSON format (an array of expectation objects). SSE streaming responses in the fixture are replayed with Server-Sent Events.

path.description: File path to the fixture JSON file to load. Must be a valid MockServer expectations JSON file.

strict.description: Strict VCR mode: register a low-priority catch-all per cassette path so a request matching no recorded entry returns HTTP 599 instead of falling through. Defaults to the mockserver.llmVcrStrict config.

normalizeRequestBodyFields.description: Optional JSON field names to drop from each recorded request body on load, matching the remaining fields loosely (ignoring extra fields), so volatile values do not block replay.

name: mock_llm_completion
description: Creates a mock LLM completion expectation that returns a provider-correct response (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) from a high-level description of text, tool calls, and usage

provider.description: LLM provider with a registered codec (ANTHROPIC, OPENAI, OPENAI_RESPONSES, GEMINI, BEDROCK, AZURE_OPENAI, OLLAMA).

toolCalls.description: Tool/function calls to include in the response

arguments.description: Tool arguments as a JSON string or object

streaming.description: Whether to stream the response (default false)

outputSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema the response 'text' is expected to conform to. Validated as the response is encoded (fail-soft): a mismatch leaves the body unchanged but adds an 'x-mockserver-structured-output-invalid' diagnostic header and logs a warning. Accepts a JSON Schema as a string or an inline object.

enforceOutputSchema.description: Opt-in strict structured-output enforcement (default false). When true and an 'outputSchema' is set, a non-conforming configured response fails loudly with a provider-correct error (HTTP 502) instead of the fail-soft diagnostic header — modelling a provider's strict response_format:json_schema mode that guarantees schema-valid output.

chaos.description: Optional fault/chaos profile for resilience testing

errorStatus.description: HTTP error status to return (e.g. 429, 529); fires always unless errorProbability is set

retryAfter.description: Value for the Retry-After header on an injected error

errorProbability.description: Probability 0.0-1.0 of injecting the error (default 1.0 when errorStatus set)

truncateAtFraction.description: Fraction 0.0-1.0 of SSE events to keep before truncating (default 0.5)

seed.description: Seed making a fractional errorProbability reproducible

quotaName.description: Stateful quota bucket name; expectations sharing a name share one request counter

quotaLimit.description: Stateful quota: max requests allowed per window before requests are rejected

quotaWindowMillis.description: Stateful quota: window length in milliseconds

quotaErrorStatus.description: Stateful quota: HTTP status returned when the quota is exceeded (default 429)

name: create_llm_conversation
description: Creates a multi-turn LLM conversation mock with scenario-based state advancement. Each turn matches based on conversation predicates and returns a configured completion.

provider.description: LLM provider with a registered codec (ANTHROPIC, OPENAI, OPENAI_RESPONSES, GEMINI, BEDROCK, AZURE_OPENAI, OLLAMA).

source.description: Where to extract the isolation key: header, queryParameter, or cookie

name.description: Name of the header, query parameter, or cookie

turnIndex.description: Match when conversation has this many assistant turns (0-based)

latestMessageContains.description: Match when latest message contains this substring

latestMessageMatches.description: Match when latest message matches this Java regex pattern

latestMessageRole.description: Match when latest message has this role

containsToolResultFor.description: Match when conversation contains a tool result for this tool name

semanticMatchAgainst.description: Opt-in fuzzy match: the intent the latest message should express, judged by a runtime LLM. Off unless mockserver.llmSemanticMatchingEnabled is set and a backend resolves; non-deterministic, exploratory only, never for assertions

normalization.description: Optional deterministic normalisation applied to the latest-message text (and the latestMessageContains value) before matching, so cosmetic differences in dynamically-assembled prompts do not block a match

collapseWhitespace.description: Collapse runs of whitespace to a single space and trim (default true)

lowercase.description: Lowercase the text before matching (default false)

sortJsonKeys.description: When the prompt is JSON, sort object keys so key ordering is irrelevant (default true)

dropBuiltInVolatileFields.description: Strip ISO-8601 timestamps, UUIDs, and prefix_… ids (req_/msg_/call_/…) before matching (default false)

dropVolatileFields.description: Names of JSON fields to drop from the prompt before matching

arguments.description: Tool arguments as string or object

chaos.description: Optional fault/chaos profile for resilience testing

errorStatus.description: HTTP error status to return (e.g. 429, 529); fires always unless errorProbability is set

retryAfter.description: Value for the Retry-After header on an injected error

errorProbability.description: Probability 0.0-1.0 of injecting the error (default 1.0 when errorStatus set)

truncateAtFraction.description: Fraction 0.0-1.0 of SSE events to keep before truncating (default 0.5)

seed.description: Seed making a fractional errorProbability reproducible

quotaName.description: Stateful quota bucket name; expectations sharing a name share one request counter

quotaLimit.description: Stateful quota: max requests allowed per window before requests are rejected

quotaWindowMillis.description: Stateful quota: window length in milliseconds

quotaErrorStatus.description: Stateful quota: HTTP status returned when the quota is exceeded (default 429)

ids.description: Optional expectation IDs to assign per turn. Reusing the existing IDs updates the conversation in place.

name: mock_llm_failover
description: Creates an LLM failover/retry scenario: the first N requests fail with the specified HTTP statuses, then subsequent requests succeed with a provider-correct LLM response. Use this to test that retry/failover logic (LiteLLM, Envoy AI Gateway, SDK retries) works correctly.

provider.description: LLM provider with a registered codec (ANTHROPIC, OPENAI, OPENAI_RESPONSES, GEMINI, BEDROCK, AZURE_OPENAI, OLLAMA).

model.description: Model name for the success response (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4)

failStatuses.description: Ordered array of HTTP status codes — one per failure attempt (e.g. [503, 503, 429]). The first N requests return these statuses in order, then subsequent requests succeed.

toolCalls.description: Tool/function calls for the success response

arguments.description: Tool arguments as a JSON string or object

stopReason.description: Stop reason for the success response

usage.description: Token usage for the success response

name: verify_tool_call
description: Assert that an agent called a named tool (optionally with arguments matching a regex) a given number of times, by inspecting LLM requests recorded through MockServer. Works with both mock-backed and proxied/forwarded traffic.

provider.description: LLM provider whose recorded requests to inspect. Use AUTO to detect the provider from the recorded request paths (useful for proxied traffic where the provider is implicit in the upstream URL).

toolName.description: Name of the tool the agent should have called

argumentsRegex.description: Optional Java regex matched against the tool call's argument JSON

atLeast.description: Minimum number of matching tool calls required (default 1)

atMost.description: Optional maximum number of matching tool calls allowed

name: verify_structured_output
description: Validate that the structured (JSON) output of recorded LLM responses conforms to a JSON Schema. Decodes each recorded response for the given provider, extracts the assistant's output text, and checks it against the schema — use this to assert an agent (or mocked model) produced schema-valid structured output. Read-only and deterministic; responses with no text output are reported separately as skipped.

provider.description: LLM provider whose recorded responses to validate

schema.description: JSON Schema that the structured output text of each recorded response must conform to

path.description: Optional request path filter (only validate responses to this path)

name: verify_cost_budget
description: Assert that the total estimated USD cost of recorded LLM responses is within a budget. Decodes each recorded response for the given provider (via the runtime-LLM client SPI), sums input/output tokens from the reported usage, prices them with the built-in pricing table, and compares the total against maxCostUsd. Read-only and deterministic — use it as a CI cost gate for an agent run. Responses without usage are skipped; responses whose model has no known price are reported as unpriceable and excluded from the total.

provider.description: LLM provider whose recorded responses to total (must have a registered runtime client).

maxCostUsd.description: Cost budget in USD. The assertion passes when the total estimated cost of the recorded responses is at or below this value.

model.description: Optional model id used to price every response (e.g. claude-sonnet-4). If omitted, the model is read from each recorded request body, or from the path of a native Gemini call; a call sent to a Vertex AI host is priced at Vertex AI's rates. Responses whose model cannot be priced are reported as unpriceable and excluded from the total.

path.description: Optional request path filter (only total responses to this path).

name: explain_agent_run
description: Summarise an agent run reconstructed from recorded LLM requests: message and assistant-turn counts, the ordered tool-call sequence, tool results, and the latest message role. Works with both mock-backed and proxied/forwarded traffic.

provider.description: LLM provider whose recorded requests to summarise. Use AUTO to detect the provider from the recorded request paths (useful for proxied traffic where the provider is implicit in the upstream URL).

isolationType.description: Optional: scope the run to a single session by the isolation source the conversation was isolated on.

isolationKey.description: Optional: the header/query-parameter/cookie name used to isolate the session (e.g. x-agent-id).

isolationValue.description: Optional: the value identifying the session (e.g. agent-001).

name: export_optimisation_report
description: Turn captured LLM traffic (proxied through MockServer) into an optimisation export: a copy-paste Markdown 'optimisation brief' (paste into any LLM for cost-reduction advice) or the structured JSON bundle. Includes deterministic optimisation signals (repeated system prompts, large static context resent, deterministic tool calls, oversized tool results, output bloat, duplicate retries) with token and cost estimates. Export-only and deterministic — MockServer never calls an LLM. Secrets are redacted.

format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for the copy-paste optimisation brief (default), 'json' for the structured LlmOptimisationReport bundle, 'csv' for the per-call + totals spreadsheet export, or an eval/fine-tune dataset export of the captured sessions — 'openai-evals' (OpenAI-evals JSONL), 'fine-tune' (chat fine-tune JSONL), or 'promptfoo' (promptfoo test-suite JSON). All formats redact secrets.

session.description: Optional session/grouping key filter (e.g. 'host:api.openai.com'); default is all captured LLM traffic.

provider.description: Optional LLM provider filter (e.g. OPENAI, ANTHROPIC).

name: diff_agent_runs
description: Prompt-level diff of two recorded agent runs captured through MockServer. Reconstructs each run's canonical conversation, normalises the prompts (whitespace / JSON key order / volatile ids), and reports what changed: message additions / removals / edits, tool calls added or removed, and the token / cost delta. Read-only and deterministic — MockServer never calls an LLM. Message text is masked for credential shapes.

before.description: Selects the BEFORE run from captured LLM traffic by session/host/provider (same filter as export_optimisation_report).

after.description: Selects the AFTER run — same shape as 'before'.

normalization.description: Optional prompt-normalisation options (whitespace, JSON key ordering, volatile ids) applied before diffing.

name: detect_llm_drift
description: Replays a recorded LLM cassette against the live provider and reports STRUCTURAL drift in the responses (new/removed fields, type changes) — not semantic differences. Requires a configured runtime LLM backend (env vars, mockserver.llmProvider/llmApiKey, or a named backend); if none is configured the tool is disabled. Fails closed per exchange: a network error or non-2xx live response is reported as could-not-check, never as drift. Intended for an opt-in/scheduled CI lane, not the per-commit build.

cassettePath.description: Path to a recorded fixture (cassette) JSON file whose exchanges are replayed against the live provider

provider.description: LLM provider the cassette was recorded against

backendName.description: Optional named backend from mockserver.llmBackendsConfig; otherwise the default backend is resolved from env/properties

name: mock_adversarial_llm_response
description: Creates a mock LLM completion whose response is a curated ADVERSARIAL payload (prompt injection, jailbreak, data-exfiltration request, malformed/oversized content) so you can test that your agent RESISTS hostile or malformed model/tool output. Defensive testing aid — the payloads are benign test fixtures, not working exploits. Deterministic.

provider.description: LLM provider with a registered codec

payload.description: Adversarial payload id — one of the enum values below

name: list_mock_tools
description: Generates Model Context Protocol tool definitions from the current mock expectations, so an agent can discover the mocked endpoints as callable tools. Each response expectation becomes one tool (name derived from method and path, inputSchema for query parameters and request body, plus a _mockserver annotation with the target method/path).

name: list_expectations
description: Lists the currently active mock expectations, optionally filtered by a request method and/or path. Returns each expectation in the full MockServer JSON format (including its id), so an agent can inspect, modify (via create_expectation/raw_expectation) or clear (via clear_expectations) what is mocked. Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/retrieve?type=ACTIVE_EXPECTATIONS.

method.description: Optionally filter active expectations to those whose request matcher targets this HTTP method

path.description: Optionally filter active expectations to those whose request matcher targets this path

name: set_operating_mode
description: Sets the high-level operating mode of MockServer in one switch: SIMULATE (return mocks, 404 on no match), SPY (return mocks but forward+record requests that match no expectation), or CAPTURE (forward+record all traffic). SPY/CAPTURE let an agent record real upstream traffic that can then be turned into mocks via promote_recordings. Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/mode?mode=<MODE>.

mode.description: Operating mode: SIMULATE (match mocks, 404 unmatched), SPY (match mocks, forward+record unmatched), or CAPTURE (forward+record everything)

name: promote_recordings
description: Promotes traffic already recorded by MockServer's forwarding/proxy mode (e.g. after set_operating_mode SPY/CAPTURE) into ACTIVE mock expectations in one step, so an agent can "record then mock". Redacts secrets, and by default consolidates and parameterizes the recordings into reusable mocks (unlimited times). Equivalent to PUT /mockserver/recordings/promote.

method.description: Filter recorded traffic by HTTP method (e.g. GET, POST)

path.description: Filter recorded traffic by request path (e.g. /api/users)

consolidate.description: Collapse duplicate recorded exchanges into consolidated reusable mocks (default true); when false each recording is promoted verbatim

parameterize.description: When consolidating, generalise volatile path/query/header/body values so a single recorded id does not pin the mock (default true)

redactSensitiveData.description: Redact secrets (auth headers, common secret body fields) from promoted mocks (default true)
